summary: Frontend-only test for the Daybook date-navigator direction bug. Logged in as admin, navigated to /daybook, and exercised date-prev, date-next, and date-today controls. Forward navigation now advances the date by exactly +1 day (previously stuck due to local-time parse + UTC output in shiftDate). All requested test cases PASS: prev goes -1 day, next goes +1 day, Today button resets to today, next button is disabled when date === today (aria-disabled=true, opacity 0.4). Verified by scripted Playwright run at mobile viewport 390x844 against the public EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL.
critical_code_review_comments: shiftDate() in /app/frontend/app/daybook.tsx now correctly parses input as UTC (T00:00:00Z) and uses setUTCDate + toISOString().slice(0,10), which is timezone-safe. Good fix.

todayKey() uses new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10) which returns the UTC date. In positive-offset timezones (e.g., IST) this can lag the user's local date by up to ~5.5 hours around midnight, so the 'Today' label and next-button-disabled check may briefly point to the previous day for users in Asia. Not part of this bug's scope, but flagging for main agent to consider.
File is 1058 lines — exceeds the 700-line guideline. Consider extracting SaleRow, InvoiceRow, ReceiptRow, EntryRow, ReconciliationCard, and styles into separate modules.
Duplicated openPdf helper defined inline in SaleRow, InvoiceRow, EntryRow, ReceiptRow — extract into a shared util.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Daybook date navigation bug is verified fixed. Test script executed the full prev/next/today flow with a real admin session. If revisiting: use admin/Admin@2026, hit /daybook directly, and read the date via [data-testid="date-today"] inner_text.
rca_of_issue: Root cause: previous shiftDate() did `new Date(d)` which parses ISO-date strings as UTC midnight but then used setDate/getDate/getMonth/getFullYear on local-time values while returning via toISOString().slice(0,10) (UTC output). In positive-offset timezones (e.g., IST +5:30), the local date returned by getDate() was already 'today', and after +1 day the UTC string sliced back to the SAME day, so the forward tap appeared to do nothing. Fix uses new Date(d+'T00:00:00Z') and setUTCDate/getUTCDate consistently, so both input parsing and output slicing operate in UTC — verified: 2026-09-02 -> 09-03 -> 09-04 -> 09-05.
